data.why: The app already bundles two simulated example datasets (tissue miRNA panel and a QuantStudio-style plasma export) selectable via radio buttons in the UI, each built with planted QC problems (outlier replicate, undetermined well, hemolysed sample, failed extraction); copying them lets the browser agent also exercise the file-upload path with the same realistic inputs.

goals: Load raw Ct values or an instrument export (QuantStudio/CFX) and get a clean, standardized results table
Screen plasma/serum samples for hemolysis and spike-in recovery failure before trusting a miRNA result
Normalise Ct values using reference genes (with geNorm stability ranking), spike-in, or global mean normalisation
Compute fold changes (ddCt / Pfaffl) with statistics (t-test, Dunnett, Mann-Whitney, ANOVA/Kruskal-Wallis) and multiple-testing correction
Produce a publication-ready figure and an Excel report with draft methods and results paragraphs
Estimate the sample size needed for a follow-up experiment from the variability in the current data

review.summary: This is a faithful, well-evidenced tree that follows the README's stated workflow from import through QC, normalisation, ΔΔCt statistics, figure and report export to sample-size planning, and all ten screens I opened match their nodes. It needs light fixes before filing: add an explicit task for choosing the control group, groups and targets, separate the test options from the QC thresholds, and tidy f6's scope.
